interpretation: The observed bottleneck is repeated interface/permission/reference errors and lack of source handoff under this frozen public-tool/profile/context contract. It does not establish failure at SQL reasoning because no SQL was written or built.

Provider attempted twelve consecutive identical reads supplying both alias and object_id, then another invalid dual-identity audit read; no actual held evidence was read. Its attempted handoff was correctly rejected for lack of prior read.

Implementer obtained structural preflight feedback and an authorized data adoption, but made no actual data read. Basis adoption lacked sharing. Seventeen subsequent identical generic requests used alias inside a version reference instead of an object identity; these requests were rejected and did not create basis delivery.

Reviewer produced two genuine manual audit_basis requests and could wait, but did not read the basis it held or hand it to the implementer. Its dual-identity result reads failed, and an attempted handoff used a route for which it was not the provider.

The failed tool responses were present in the later actual model inputs checked here. This rules out omission of these specific returned errors as an explanation for the observed repetitions; it does not prove why the model did not adapt.

Seven successful public operations are concrete partial activity, but three successful preflight calls reported structural problems rather than readiness. No file version changed and no submission existed at the 20-decision/member cutoff.

All sixty actual completions retain token traces and complete per-member actor trajectories in the frozen exporter. V is false due missing work basis/delivery; truthful eligible reward0 is retained as a base-training failure. This single-case data eligibility is not a parameter-update or learning-improvement result.
No protocol, source, prompt, reward, world or sampling schedule was changed; the rest of the predeclared queue continues.
